records.mutation: make the anti-case-split clause executable: one divisor table as the first move, plus rival-elimination check
records.subagent_summary: Train reward was 1/8; seven failures shared one pattern: the student read "I do not know" as merely "the revealed number has several factor pairs", which discriminates nothing, then committed to an arbitrary mid-sized factor pair, and several first split into external sum-vs-product cases and declared one contradictory despite the incumbent forbidding it. The edit keeps the incumbent's proven framing but replaces the abstract no-case-split and verify clauses with an executable first move (one table of own-values x, ambiguity requires both readings legal so x must divide N) and a rival-elimination check, and is slightly shorter than the incumbent.

records.mutation: replace unused algebra micro-step with a broader locus/aggregate trigger
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with finish_reason stop and no truncation, so the hint's first move, the k-trap and the commit-and-stop rule are all working and were left verbatim. Clause-level inspection showed zero rollouts used the 'collect the x^2+y^2 terms, divide by their coefficient' micro-step (they went straight from squaring to completing the square), so that dead clause was deleted and its tokens spent widening the opening trigger from the narrow 'all roots lie on one circle' phrasing to any locus-or-aggregate request, targeting the weak held-out transfer rather than the already-saturated training score. Total length is unchanged at 198 tokens, so the shared book does not grow.

records.mutation: name the quadrilateral-vs-triangle clipping trap; drop redundant trust clause
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 1/8 with 6 of 8 truncating at the 16384-token cap: the student repeatedly looped hunting for a rotation that shrinks the overlap instead of finishing one numeric case. The two that terminated both reduced the clipped region to a triangle through the two exit rays, dropping the small-square corner that lies between them, so one reported a too-small overlap. The edit replaces the vague per-angle instruction with an explicit axis-parallel first move and a named clipping trap (include every enclosed corner; the region is usually a quadrilateral), and deletes the redundant trust-the-shoelace clause to stay near the incumbent length.

records.mutation: pin deg(P-L)=n exactly (not n-1) and forbid retreating from the matched bound
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 3/8 with two dominant, distinct failure modes: three rollouts mis-set deg(P-L)=n-1 instead of n and so undercounted the per-polynomial root cap, while two others derived the correct cap but then abandoned it, arguing that consecutive inputs force each polynomial to be used only once. One rollout looped to the token cap after concluding impossibility. The edit keeps the proven affine-target/root-counting skeleton and replaces only the vague "compare degrees to show g is not identically zero" clause with the exact leading-coefficient argument, plus a short guard against retreating from an already-matched bound.

records.mutation: swap the vague sign-flip warning for a concrete root self-test with targeted recovery
records.subagent_summary: All three failures (3/8) hit the 16384-token cap after deriving the same offset direction backwards, producing a negative discriminant and then spending 6000+ tokens doubting the curve parameters and the parallelogram reading instead of the one conversion line; the incumbent told them the flip was the dominant failure mode but gave no way to detect it. The revision names an executable detector (a given vertex must be a root of the reduced scalar equation) plus a one-line recovery, and drops the diffuse do-not-restart wording to stay shorter than the incumbent.

records.mutation: replace vague 'trace the realizing sequences' with the concrete conditioning move: count loading moves before the first delivery move
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts scored 0, but not from truncation or bad arithmetic: 6 of 8 correctly derived the first sub-answer via the state/forced-move accounting the incumbent already teaches, then answered the second sub-part with a bare 1/n symmetry claim, which the grader reads as the emitted value. They also all reached the correct last-in-first-out timing claim but had no executable way to identify WHICH item satisfies it, so they defaulted to symmetry despite the incumbent's explicit prohibition. I therefore replaced the vague 'trace only the move sequences that realize that event' clause with the concrete conditioning step (count the loading moves preceding the first delivery move), keeping the proven state-graph, timing-claim, anti-symmetry, and commit clauses and holding length at the incumbent's 146-147 tokens.

records.mutation: replace abstract Lagrange/verify clauses with one explicit test-polynomial construction plus a stop rule
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 0/8 with 7 of 8 truncating at the 16384-token cap: the student latched onto the functional framing but never had an executable first move, so it churned on Vandermonde inversion and on self-contradictory small analogues (wrong equation/unknown counts) until it ran out of room, and the several rollouts that did emit a value had silently swapped node index for exponent. I therefore kept the proven functional/moment framing and the product-of-node-differences endpoint, but swapped the vague 'apply Lagrange interpolation after any useful index shift' and the verify-the-highest-moment clause (no rollout followed either productively; the latter fed the looping) for a single concrete construction plus an explicit no-restart, commit-and-stop rule.

records.mutation: replace problem-specific layout clause with general no-extra-constraint rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8/8 rollouts were correct with finish_reason stop and no truncation, so the divisibility + maximum-count + multiplicative-markup core is proven and untouched. The one clause the rollouts implicated as harmful was the assertion that the layout constrains H arithmetically: rollouts revisited that wording 1 to 41 times each, repeatedly asking what constraint it imposed before concluding it imposed none, which is pure wasted budget. I replaced that single clause with a general rule that grouping/layout wording adds no constraint unless it forces divisibility, and generalized 'stage' to 'component' for transfer, keeping the hint at the same length (76 vs 77 tokens).

records.mutation: swap unused branch-elimination clause for a warning against pinning coefficients from a single x
records.subagent_summary: 6 of 8 rollouts were correct; both failures shared one mechanism: after correctly deriving the affine link they abandoned coefficient matching and instead plugged a single x value into the commuting identity, which under-determines the system, produced a huge spurious coefficient, and led to one non-terminating rollout (hit the 16384-token cap) and one confidently wrong result. Meanwhile the incumbent clause telling the student not to explore the q = p + constant branch is dead weight - essentially no rollout ever pursued that branch - so I deleted it and spent those tokens on the concrete trap the rollouts actually fell into, keeping total length at the incumbent's.

records.mutation: replace unused bit-string clause with the observed order-2 involution trap
records.subagent_summary: 3/8 correct; the two cleanest wins came from pure explicit list tracing plus orbit tracking and never touched the binary/bit-string clause, while three of five failures collapsed to the same fallacy of calling the composite a product of disjoint transpositions and asserting order 2, and two failures looped to the token cap while trying to reconcile a bit-string model. I therefore deleted the bit-string verification clause no winning rollout used and spent fewer tokens on an explicit warning that the overlapping stages do not compose into disjoint swaps and the composite is not self-inverse, keeping the proven first move, invariant check, trust-the-trace rule and commit-and-stop ending intact.
